meta.docSubtitle: 4 flows · Salesforce + QuickBooks + Inventory · Most answers are pre-filled — please verify and correct

bizContext.snapshot: AgileMind (Test) is a K-12 educational publisher in Grapevine, TX (~$18M ARR) selling print curriculum materials (Student Activity Books) to ~300 school districts through Salesforce. QuickBooks handles invoicing and inventory costs. Holly Wale tracks demand inventory in a manual spreadsheet. DataSkate connects these three systems in 4 integration flows — eliminating Crystal's daily manual billing loop and placing inventory visibility directly in Salesforce. Most answers in this form are already filled in from your discovery calls. Your job is to confirm they are correct and fill in the blanks we genuinely couldn't know.

journeyCards.label: Phase 1 — Connected
journeyCards.headline: Agreement-to-Invoice and Inventory in One View
journeyCards.body: Crystal stops manually creating QuickBooks invoices — agreements fire invoices automatically. Payment status syncs back to Salesforce. Holly's inventory spreadsheet flows into Salesforce Inventory__c. Maria can answer cost-per-program questions in Salesforce without opening QuickBooks.

journeyCards.label: Phase 2 — Automated
journeyCards.headline: Shortage Alerts and Fulfillment Triggers Fire Themselves
journeyCards.body: When available inventory for a title drops below Holly's 3% buffer threshold, a Salesforce alert fires automatically to Holly and the responsible sales rep — before the shortage becomes a fulfillment problem at back-to-school.

journeyCards.label: Phase 3 — AgentForce
journeyCards.headline: Maria's Question Answered in 5 Seconds
journeyCards.body: 'What have we spent on Intensified Algebra Vol 1 over the last five years?' — an AgentForce agent reads the Inventory__c records and Invoice history Phase 1 builds and answers in Salesforce. No call to Holly required. That architecture is decided once.

p0Blockers.title: QuickBooks Version (Q14)
p0Blockers.clientAction: — The entire integration architecture changes based on this answer. QBO (web) vs Desktop (installed) determines the connector path. Maria or Crystal can confirm which version is in use.

p0Blockers.title: Holly's Spreadsheet Storage Location (Q6)
p0Blockers.clientAction: — The connector path for UC3 depends entirely on where Holly's file lives. Local laptop cannot work with cloud integration — the file must be in Google Drive, SharePoint, or OneDrive. Holly or Chloe (IT) to confirm.

p0Blockers.title: Chloe (IT Director) Contact Info (Q13)
p0Blockers.clientAction: — Chloe provisions all three credential flows: Salesforce Connected App, Google Service Account (if Google Sheets), and Azure AD app registration (if SharePoint). All three paths are blocked without her last name and email.

sections.title: Use Cases & Integration Flows
sections.bodyHtml:
UC1

Salesforce Agreement → QuickBooks Invoice Creation

▼

Salesforce → QuickBooks · HIGH complexity · Trigger: Platform Event or CDC on Agreement (Closed Won)

Business problem: Crystal Robinson manually creates the QuickBooks invoice after each Salesforce Agreement is closed — re-entering account details, line items, and product details that already exist in Salesforce. This flow eliminates that manual step entirely.

1

When a new Agreement is created in Salesforce — does that always mean a signed district PO is in hand, or does the Agreement sometimes get created before the PO arrives? K-12 district invoicing requires a valid PO before an invoice can be legally accepted (FKC-004 pattern) — if Agreements are created speculatively before PO receipt, a confirmation gate is needed before UC1 fires.

2

How does the team currently resolve the correct ISBN for each line item — is there a lookup table (state × product → ISBN), or does someone look this up manually?

3

QB Customer matching: do QuickBooks Customer names match Salesforce Account names exactly (e.g., Austin ISD in SF = Austin ISD in QB)? If there are mismatches, is a QB Customer ID stored anywhere on the Salesforce Account?

In ScopeCreate a QuickBooks invoice with line items when a Salesforce Agreement reaches Closed Won; stamp the QB Invoice ID back to the Agreement record (QB_InvoiceId__c)
Assumes Pre-existsQB Customer records for all AgileMind (Test) school districts already in QuickBooks; Salesforce Opportunity stages and Agreement custom object already exist; CDC or Platform Events enabled on Agreement (see Q54)
Out of ScopeCreating new QB Customer records for new districts; QB payment processing; Salesforce licensing or AgentForce enablement
UC2

QuickBooks Invoice Status → Salesforce Agreement Sync

▼

QuickBooks → Salesforce · MEDIUM complexity · Trigger: Scheduled poll (QB invoices by LastModifiedDate, April 1 fiscal year offset)

Business problem: Crystal manually checks QuickBooks for payment status and copies invoice number, payment date, and open balance back to the Salesforce Agreement. This flow polls QuickBooks on a schedule and writes that data back automatically.

4

How frequently should payment status sync from QuickBooks to Salesforce?

5

Which fields should sync from QuickBooks to the Salesforce Agreement?

In ScopeScheduled sync of QB invoice payment status to Salesforce Agreement fields; idempotent upsert via QB_InvoiceId__c external ID
Assumes Pre-existsQB_InvoiceId__c external ID field on Salesforce Agreement (DataSkate creates in sprint scope)
Out of ScopeReal-time webhook-based payment notifications; automated payment processing in QB; AR escalation email drafting (Phase 3 — AgentForce)
UC3

Holly's Demand Worksheet → Salesforce Inventory__c

▼

Spreadsheet → Salesforce · MEDIUM complexity · Trigger: Scheduled poll (connector TBD on Q6 storage location)

Business problem: Holly's inventory demand worksheet is the only place AgileMind (Test) tracks quantities on hand, committed stock, and projected shorts. Leadership cannot answer inventory questions without calling Holly directly. This flow loads that data into Salesforce Inventory__c on a schedule.

⚠️ P0 Blocker — Q6 Required Before Build Starts

The connector path (Google Sheets vs Microsoft Excel Online) depends on where Holly's file is stored. Confirm Q6 before any development begins.

6

⚠️ P0 — Where is Holly Wale's inventory demand worksheet stored?

7

What are the exact column header names in Holly's worksheet? DataWeave mapping depends on exact spelling and case — a sample row export is ideal.

8

How frequently is Holly's worksheet updated — continuously throughout the day, or once at end of day?

In ScopeScheduled sync from Holly's spreadsheet into Salesforce Inventory__c; UC3 owns: QuantityOnHand__c, QuantityCommitted__c, QuantityAvailable__c, BufferThreshold__c, ProjectedShort__c; DataSkate creates the Inventory__c object schema in this sprint
Assumes Pre-existsHolly's worksheet structure exists and column headers are stable; Google Service Account (if Google Sheets) or Azure AD app registration (if SharePoint) provisioned by Chloe
Out of ScopeFile migration from local laptop to cloud storage (IT responsibility if needed); automated shortage alerts (Phase 2); Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 licensing
UC4

QuickBooks Inventory Items → Salesforce Inventory__c (Cost Data)

▼

QuickBooks → Salesforce · MEDIUM complexity · Trigger: Scheduled poll of QB Inventory Items (runs after UC3)

Business problem: Maria cannot answer the 5-year spend question on Intensified Algebra without manually cross-referencing QuickBooks. This flow pulls QB inventory item cost data into the same Salesforce Inventory__c object UC3 writes to — enabling cost-per-program analysis directly in Salesforce.

9

In QuickBooks, what type of Item represents your print curriculum materials — Inventory Part, Non-Inventory Part, or Service?

10

Should UC4 sync include only physical print book inventory, or also digital access / license items?

In ScopeScheduled sync of QB inventory item cost data to Salesforce Inventory__c; UC4 owns: UnitCost__c, QB_ItemId__c; runs after UC3 to prevent field overwrite
Assumes Pre-existsQB Items already created for all curriculum titles (confirmed in discovery); Inventory__c object created as part of UC3 sprint scope
Out of ScopeQB purchase order creation; historical cost data backfill; multi-currency cost reporting

Potential Flows — Not Priced in This Proposal

IDFlowPriorityWhy It MattersIn Scope for This Engagement?
UC5Product Catalog Sync — Salesforce ↔ QuickBooksHigh — dependency riskMaria adds new titles to QB and Salesforce separately. Divergence silently breaks UC1 line item matching and UC4 cost lookup for new titles.
UC6CCR Pre-Fulfillment FlagMediumSales ships materials on CCRs before an Agreement is closed — UC1 would create a duplicate invoice. A CCR flag on the Agreement prevents double-billing.
UC7Inventory Decrement on FulfillmentMediumUC4's scheduled sync means Salesforce Inventory__c shows stale counts between runs. A real-time decrement event keeps Holly's dashboard accurate mid-day.

internalFlags.bodyHtml:
FLAG-1 — HIGH — QuickBooks OAuth 100-Day Expiry
QBO OAuth refresh tokens expire after 100 days of non-use. If not handled, production sync breaks silently after the first refresh window. Kailash must specify automated token refresh strategy — either Secrets Manager rotation or MuleSoft OAuth2 provider with token refresh endpoint configured. This is the single highest operational risk in this engagement.
FLAG-2 — MEDIUM — UC3/UC4 Field Ownership Conflict
UC3 and UC4 both write to Salesforce Inventory__c. Confirmed split: UC3 owns QuantityOnHand, QuantityCommitted, QuantityAvailable, BufferThreshold, ProjectedShort; UC4 owns UnitCost, QB_ItemId. Must be documented in scaffold DWL before build starts. UC4 must run after UC3 in the same scheduling window.
FLAG-3 — MEDIUM — UC1 Trigger Timing (PO Receipt vs Agreement Creation)
Agreement Created must imply a signed district PO in hand (FKC-004 pattern). If Agreements are sometimes created ahead of PO receipt, UC1 would generate a QB invoice that the district cannot legally accept. Q1 in this intake addresses this directly — do not begin UC1 build until confirmed.
FLAG-4 — MEDIUM — Chloe (IT Director) Identity Unknown
Chloe (IT Director) is the provisioner for all three credential flows: Salesforce Connected App, Google Service Account (if Google Sheets), Azure AD app registration (if SharePoint). Her last name and email are unknown. Q13 and Q46 are the unlock — do not proceed to environment setup until Chloe is identified.
FLAG-5 — MEDIUM — UC5-Potential is a UC1/UC4 Dependency Risk
Maria adds new curriculum titles to QB and Salesforce separately. Without sync, the QB Item list and SF Product catalog will diverge — UC1 line item matching and UC4 cost lookups will silently fail for new titles. Must be resolved before go-live on UC1 and UC4.
FLAG-6 — LOW — Education Canonical Models Are Stubs
Education vertical canonical models (canonical-invoice.yaml, canonical-inventory-record.yaml) are stubs derived from OAGIS. Appropriate for AgileMind (Test) scope. Promote to versioned schemas after delivery. SIF (Schools Interoperability Framework) is the closest formal K-12 data standard for future reference.
FLAG-7 — INFO — Buyer Profile (Operational Pragmatist)
Primary: Operational Pragmatist. Secondary: ROI-First Analytical. Caller: Maria Gonzalez-Pettway (Finance Director). Economic buyer: Linda. Skepticism signals present. Ivy probe: Once you have finished your vendor conversations, how does the final decision typically work — is this yours to make, or does it need sign-off from a broader team?
